draft.title: Thought reform and mass campaigns
card: After 1949 the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) used mass campaigns to build support, remove opponents and control how people thought. Ordinary people were urged to join in, often through public meetings.
Three Antis
launched in 1951 against corruption, waste and bureaucracy among officials and managers. It aimed to make the new state's workers loyal and honest.
Five Antis
launched in 1952 against bribery, tax evasion, theft of state property, cheating on government contracts and stealing economic secrets. It mainly targeted business owners.
Thought reform
meant forcing people, such as teachers and writers, to study CCP ideas, confess their faults in public and criticise their old views. Fear of being denounced pushed many to conform.
draft.remember: Early 1950s campaigns used public pressure to punish officials and business owners and to make people follow CCP ideas.

a.q: Which target best matches the Five Antis campaign of 1952?
opts: Business owners accused of bribery and tax evasion
Landlords accused of owning too much farmland
Soldiers accused of disobeying orders in Korea
Peasants accused of leaving their communes
a.why: The Five Antis aimed mainly at business owners, over matters such as bribery and tax evasion. Landlords are a tempting answer, but they were the target of land reform, not this campaign.
a.clue: Think of who ran private firms and paid taxes.

b.q: In 1952 a Shanghai teacher is made to confess his old views in public and promise to study CCP ideas. What was the main aim of this treatment?
opts: To change how he thought and make him conform
To give his school land to local peasants
To raise output in the nation's heavy industry
To punish him for cheating on a state contract
b.why: Public confession and forced study are marks of thought reform, which aimed to change beliefs and secure conformity. Cheating on a state contract fits the Five Antis, which targeted business owners, and a teacher's confession is not about that.
b.clue: Confession and study aim at beliefs, not property or business.

a.best: Business owners accused of bribery and tax evasion

b.best: To change how he thought and make him conform

problems.detail: The clue 'Think of who ran private firms and paid taxes' points straight at business owners, so a student can pick the answer without knowing the Five Antis.
The clue 'Confession and study aim at beliefs, not property or business' practically restates the right option and rules out every distractor, which gives the answer away.
